Series::sort_pair¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

std::pair<Series, Series> Series::sort_pair(
    std::int64_t dim = -1,
    bool descending = false,
    bool stable = false) const

Ordering Values Without Losing Their Origin¶

sort_pair() orders every lane of one axis and returns the ordered values together with the source positions that supplied them. .first is the value Series; .second is an int64 Series of local indices. For every output coordinate q, the defining relationship is:

result.first[q] == self gathered at result.second[q] along dim

Use this form when an ordering must also be applied to aligned data, or when a later step needs to explain where an ordered value came from. Use sort() when values alone are sufficient and argsort() when only the permutation is needed.

The two outputs come from one ordering kernel. This matters for equal values: running a value sort and an independent index sort could otherwise choose different valid orders when stability is disabled.

Parameters And Shape¶

Parameter

Meaning

Default

dim

Axis ordered independently; negative axes count from the end.

-1

descending

false orders low to high; true orders high to low.

false

stable

Preserve source order among equivalent values.

false

Both outputs retain the receiver’s shape and platform. Values retain its dtype; indices are int64. The receiver is not mutated. Ordering a non-final axis may return strided, non-contiguous outputs because the kernel moves that axis temporarily and then restores the original axis order.

With stable=false, equivalent values have no promised relative order. With stable=true, their indices remain in source order. NaN values sort after finite values in ascending order and before them in descending order. Complex values have no total ordering and are rejected.

Reverse Mode And Cost¶

The value channel is differentiable. Reverse mode scatters each incoming sensitivity back through the exact index in .second; the integer index channel is discrete. CPU execution performs one sort per lane and writes both outputs in that pass. A stable sort can require more work than an unstable sort, so request it only when equal-value provenance is part of the contract.

Examples¶

1. Order Rows And Keep Their Column Positions¶

auto table = pluss::make_series({
    {4.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0},
    {3.0, 5.0, 0.0, 5.0},
});
auto result = table.sort_pair();
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2, 4, 4],
  [0, 3, 5, 5]]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 3, 0, 2],
  [2, 0, 1, 3]]

The first row’s ordered values came from columns 1, 3, 0, 2.

2. Order Down Columns, Descending And Stable¶

auto result = table.sort_pair(0, true, true);
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[1,2], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=false)
data=[[4, 5, 4, 5],
  [3, 1, 0, 2]]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[1,2], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=false)
data=[[0, 1, 0, 1],
  [1, 0, 1, 0]]

Each column is an independent two-element lane. The restored layout is strided because axis 0, rather than the final axis, was ordered.

3. Reverse Mode Uses The Returned Permutation¶

auto x = pluss::make_series({3.0, 1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
auto result = x.sort_pair();
(result.first * pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0})).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "indices=" << result.second << "\ndx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

indices=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 0]
dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[30, 10, 20]

The weight attached to each sorted rank returns to the source position named by the paired index.

An undefined receiver, rank-zero receiver, out-of-range axis, or complex dtype is rejected. Empty lanes are valid for sorting and produce empty outputs.
